post.summary: Makes a grant, as CreateAccessGrant does.

delete.summary: Deletes a grant, as DeleteAccessGrant does.

post.summary: Makes the account's instance, as CreateAccessGrantsInstance does.

delete.summary:
Deletes the account's instance, as DeleteAccessGrantsInstance does:
one without locations only.

post.summary: Registers a location, as CreateAccessGrantsLocation does.

put.summary: Changes a location's role, as UpdateAccessGrantsLocation does.

delete.summary:
Deletes a location, as DeleteAccessGrantsLocation does: one without
grants only.

get.summary:
The actor's account's public access block, as S3 Control's
GetPublicAccessBlock gets it: `null` if it has none.

put.summary:
Sets the actor's account's public access block, which every one of its
buckets gets too, as S3 Control's PutPublicAccessBlock does.

delete.summary:
Removes the actor's account's public access block: only its buckets'
own apply.

post.summary:
Makes a member account, with `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` (as
CreateAccount).

delete.summary:
Closes a member account, at once (it must have no buckets): its users,
roles and sessions are no one from then on.

put.summary: Moves an account to the root or a unit.

post.summary: Assigns a permission set to a directory user or group, in an account.

delete.summary:
Removes an assignment: the sessions it let in lose the permission set at
once.

get.summary:
Where the backup is, and how far it's got, as `cairn backup status`
says.

put.summary:
Turns the backup on, or changes where to or how, as `cairn backup
enable` does: a new location starts a new backup, from a base.

delete.summary:
Stops backing up, as `cairn backup disable` does: what's in the bucket
stays, and turning it back on there carries on.

post.summary:
Runs a cycle of the backup within seconds (after a base, if asked), as
`cairn backup now` does.

get.summary: The account's jobs, newest first (`s3:ListJobs`).

post.summary:
Makes a job, as CreateJob does (`s3:CreateJob`, and `iam:PassRole` on
its role).

put.summary: Sets a job's priority, as UpdateJobPriority does.
Confirms or cancels a job, as UpdateJobStatus does.

delete.summary: Deletes an empty bucket.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's ACL, as PutBucketAcl does: refused with ACLs
disabled, and a public one with BlockPublicAcls.
Sets a bucket's CORS configuration, checked as PutBucketCors checks it.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's CORS configuration: no other site's page may use it.

get.summary:
An object's data, as a file to save. It's always sent as an attachment of
no particular type, so that a browser never renders it as part of the UI.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to download; the current one if not given.

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's default encryption, checked as PutBucketEncryption
checks it.

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's default encryption: new writes are encrypted only if
they ask; what's written stays as it is.

get.summary: A bucket's inventory configurations, by their IDs, and their reports.

put.summary:
Sets an inventory configuration, as S3's PutBucketInventoryConfiguration
does: its reports go to the destination as S3 writes them, so the
destination's policy must allow `s3.amazonaws.com` to write them.

delete.summary: Deletes an inventory configuration; a report of it in progress stops.

get.summary:
A bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration
gives them, but in the form they're stored in.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's
PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration does, which starts a new sweep of them.
Rules without an ID get one.

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's DeleteBucketLifecycle does:
nothing expires from then on.

put.summary:
Logs a bucket's requests into another, as PutBucketLogging does: the
target must be the same account's. Its policy must let
`logging.s3.amazonaws.com` write them, or they aren't delivered, as in S3.

delete.summary:
Turns a bucket's server access logging off, as PutBucketLogging does
with an empty `<BucketLoggingStatus>`.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's notification configurations, as S3's
PutBucketNotificationConfiguration does: each topic must let S3 publish
the bucket's events; each is sent S3's test event.

Writes an object from the request's body, as PutObject does (with the
bucket's default encryption, and as the user for SSE-KMS); its
`Content-Type` is the object's. At most 5 GiB, as a single PutObject.

parameters.name: storage_class
parameters.description:
The storage class to write it in (see `classes`); STANDARD if not
given.

delete.summary: Deletes a key, or one of its versions, as DeleteObject does.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The version to remove for good; without it, the key is deleted as
DeleteObject does (a delete marker, in a versioned bucket).

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's Object Lock configuration, as PutObjectLockConfiguration
does: enables Object Lock (on a versioned bucket only, for good), and
sets or removes its default retention.

Replaces a version's ACL, as PutObjectAcl does: refused with ACLs
disabled, and a public one with BlockPublicAcls.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version; the current one if not given.

get.summary:
What each version of a key has besides its data: its storage class,
checksum, retention, legal hold and ACL.

put.summary: Places or lifts a version's legal hold, as PutObjectLegalHold does.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version; the current one if not given.

put.summary:
Sets a version's retention, as PutObjectRetention does: it may only be
lengthened, but for one in GOVERNANCE mode, with the bypass.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version; the current one if not given.

post.summary:
Moves a key's current version into another storage class, as S3 does
it: a CopyObject onto itself that names the class, which makes a new
version (in a versioned bucket; else it replaces it), with the same
data, metadata, tags and encryption. Into a lower class, it shares the
version's bytes; into another, they're written again (see `classes`).
As CopyObject, at most 5 GiB, and not of an SSE-C version, whose key
Cairn doesn't have.

put.summary:
Replaces a version's tags, as PutObjectTagging does (or, with none,
DeleteObjectTagging).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version whose tags to set; the current one if not given.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Also list keys whose current version is a delete marker.

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's Object Ownership, as PutBucketOwnershipControls does:
disabling ACLs is refused while the bucket's ACL grants anyone but its
owner anything.

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's ownership controls, as DeleteBucketOwnershipControls
does: ACLs are enabled, and writers own what they write.

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's policy, as PutBucketPolicy does: checked as S3 checks
it, and refused if it's public while public policies are blocked.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's policy.

put.summary: Sets a bucket's public access block, as PutPublicAccessBlock does.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's public access block: only its account's applies.

get.summary:
A bucket's replication configuration, and what's queued for its
destinations.

put.summary:
Sets a bucket's replication configuration, checked as
PutBucketReplication checks it: the bucket and its destinations must be
versioned, a remote's bucket is asked there, and the caller must be
allowed to pass the role (`iam:PassRole`).

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's replication configuration: nothing more is queued,
and what's queued fails.

get.summary:
What's queued of a key's versions, by destination: to whom may read the
object and its bucket's replication configuration, which names the
destinations; older versions' only to whom may list them.

The remotes (`cairn remote`) the bucket's rules can name, to whom may
set its configuration: PutBucketReplication's errors tell them which
remotes there are anyway ("There's no remote …").

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's tags, as PutBucketTagging does (or, with none,
DeleteBucketTagging).

post.summary:
Starts a multipart upload, as CreateMultipartUpload does: for a file
larger than one upload may be (5 GiB), in parts.

delete.summary: Aborts a multipart upload, as AbortMultipartUpload does: its parts go.

post.summary:
Completes a multipart upload with its parts, in order, as
CompleteMultipartUpload does: the object is written then.

put.summary:
Uploads one part (1 to 10000) of a multipart upload, from the request's
body: at least 5 MiB but for the last, at most 5 GiB.
Enables or suspends a bucket's versioning, as PutBucketVersioning does.

Sets a bucket's website configuration, checked as PutBucketWebsite
checks it.

delete.summary: Removes a bucket's website configuration: its website serves nothing.

get.summary: The nodes, each with the metrics it reports, if it's live.
The identity store's groups.

post.summary: Makes a group of Cairn's own directory, as identitystore's CreateGroup.

put.summary: Changes a group of Cairn's own directory, as identitystore's UpdateGroup.

delete.summary:
Deletes a group of Cairn's own directory: its memberships and
assignments go too.

post.summary:
Puts a directory user (any, a source's too) in a group of Cairn's own
directory, as identitystore's CreateGroupMembership.

delete.summary:
Takes a user out of a group of Cairn's own directory, by the
membership's ID, as identitystore's DeleteGroupMembership.

get.summary:
The identity store's users: Cairn's own directory's, and those of
identity sources that have signed in, most recent first.

post.summary:
Makes a user of Cairn's own directory, as identitystore's CreateUser:
it signs in with passkeys, the first of which it makes with a setup
link.

put.summary: Changes a user of Cairn's own directory, as identitystore's UpdateUser.

delete.summary:
Deletes a user of Cairn's own directory: its memberships, assignments,
passkeys and sessions go too.

Removes all of a directory user's passkeys, as when one is lost: its
sessions end, and it needs a setup link to sign in again.

post.summary:
Makes a user of Cairn's own directory a setup link, valid 7 days, to
make a passkey with (its first, or another): Cairn's way of Identity
Center's one-time password. It replaces the user's last link. Checked as
`identitystore:UpdateUser`, as a change of how the user signs in.

Hands a directory user credentials of its permission set's role, for its
session duration, as Identity Center's access portal does. They work
until they expire, whatever becomes of the console's session.
Has a directory user's session act as one of its permission sets.

Gives a directory user of Cairn's own directory a passkey with its setup
link (using the link up), and signs in with it.

200.description: Signed in; the session's cookie is set

post.summary: Makes a group, as IAM's CreateGroup.

delete.summary:
Deletes a group, unless it has members or policies left, as IAM's
DeleteGroup.

patch.summary:
Renames or moves a group, as IAM's UpdateGroup: checked on it, and on
where it goes.

post.summary: Attaches a managed policy to a group.

delete.summary: Detaches a managed policy from a group.

put.summary: Adds a user to a group, as IAM's AddUserToGroup (checked on the group).

delete.summary: Removes a user from a group, as IAM's RemoveUserFromGroup.

get.summary: One of the group's inline policies.

put.summary: Sets one of the group's inline policies, if it's a valid identity policy.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the group's inline policies.

post.summary:
Adds a provider, as IAM's CreateOpenIDConnectProvider: after checking
its issuer can be reached (its discovery document and keys).

put.summary:
Changes a provider's client IDs, thumbprints and tags, as IAM's
Add/RemoveClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider,
UpdateOpenIDConnectProviderThumbprint and Tag/UntagOpenIDConnectProvider
would.

delete.summary:
Deletes a provider: its web identities assume no role any more (the
trust policies naming it stay, and match no one).

get.summary:
How lifecycle sweeps are going: the rate, how long a round takes at it,
and each bucket's sweep.

post.summary: Signs in with a passkey, as its directory user.

200.description: Signed in; the session's cookie is set

post.summary: Signs out: ends the session.

204.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared

post.summary:
Keeps a node that's being removed, or was, as `cairn node keep` does: it
gets shards again; those that moved stay where they are.

Starts removing a node, as `cairn node remove` does: it gets no new
shards, and its shards move to the other nodes (see `mover`).

put.summary: Sets an OIDC provider, after checking its discovery document and keys.

delete.summary:
Removes an OIDC provider: its directory users, their sessions, and the
assignments to them and its groups go too.

get.summary:
Where providers send the browser back to (register it with them): ends
the sign-in, as the directory user the provider vouches for, and goes on
to the console, replacing the browser's session if it had one. One with
no permission set assigned to it, or its groups, doesn't get in.

303.description: On to the console, signed in (or to the sign-in page, with what went wrong)

get.summary: The OIDC providers people may sign in at (for the sign-in page).

post.summary: Starts a sign-in at an identity source, as a directory user.
Makes a service control policy (attached nowhere yet).

get.summary: A service control policy's document.

put.summary: Changes a service control policy: at once, wherever it's attached.

delete.summary: Deletes a service control policy, which must be attached nowhere.

post.summary: Attaches a service control policy to the root, a unit or an account.

delete.summary: Detaches a service control policy from a target, which must keep one.

put.summary:
Enables service control policies: FullAWSAccess is attached to the
root, every unit and every account.

delete.summary: Disables service control policies: every SCP is detached.

post.summary:
Makes an organizational unit, in the root or another unit (five deep at
most).

put.summary: Renames an organizational unit.

delete.summary: Deletes an organizational unit, which must be empty.

post.summary: Adds a passkey to the signed-in user of Cairn's own directory.

put.summary: Renames one of the signed-in directory user's passkeys.

delete.summary:
Removes one of the signed-in directory user's passkeys (not its last),
and ends the sessions signed in with it.

post.summary: Makes a permission set, and its role.

put.summary: Changes a permission set's description and session duration.

delete.summary: Deletes a permission set: its assignments and its roles go too.

post.summary: Attaches a managed policy (AWS's, or the account's) to a permission set.

delete.summary: Detaches a managed policy from a permission set.

put.summary:
Sets a permission set's permissions boundary: a managed policy (AWS's,
or the account's).

delete.summary: Removes a permission set's permissions boundary.

get.summary: A permission set's inline policy.

put.summary: Sets a permission set's inline policy.

delete.summary: Removes a permission set's inline policy.

post.summary:
Provisions a permission set again to every account it's provisioned to,
as sso-admin's `ProvisionPermissionSet` for `ALL_PROVISIONED_ACCOUNTS`:
their roles hold it as it is now. For a set whose roles don't, as when
it was changed by a session that may not provision it, or through
sso-admin.

put.summary: Makes one of a managed policy's versions its default (a rollback, say).
Sets a managed policy's tags, as IAM's TagPolicy and UntagPolicy would.

get.summary: A managed policy's versions (up to five), newest first.

delete.summary: Deletes one of a managed policy's versions, but its default.

get.summary:
The replication remotes, and the buckets whose rules name each, as
`cairn remote list` lists them.

post.summary: Adds a replication remote, as `cairn remote add` does.

put.summary: Changes a replication remote, as `cairn remote set` does.

delete.summary:
Deletes a replication remote that no bucket's rules name, as `cairn
remote delete` does.

post.summary: Makes a role, as IAM's CreateRole.

delete.summary: Deletes a role, unless it has policies left, as IAM's DeleteRole.

patch.summary: Changes a role's description or longest session, as IAM's UpdateRole.

post.summary: Attaches a managed policy to a role.

delete.summary: Detaches a managed policy from a role.

put.summary: Sets a role's permissions boundary.

delete.summary: Removes a role's permissions boundary.

get.summary: One of the role's inline policies.

put.summary: Sets one of the role's inline policies, if it's a valid identity policy.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the role's inline policies.

post.summary:
Revokes the role's sessions issued until now, as AWS's console does: an
inline policy `AWSRevokeOlderSessions` that denies everything to
sessions whose token was issued before now (`aws:TokenIssueTime`). New
sessions aren't affected; doing it again moves the time.

put.summary: Sets a role's tags, as IAM's TagRole and UntagRole would.
Sets a role's trust policy, as IAM's UpdateAssumeRolePolicy.

post.summary:
Signs in as the account's root user, with a link the command line on a
node made (`cairn account root-link`), which it uses up. The session is
short (an hour at most), and not multi-factor.

200.description: Signed in as the root user; the session's cookie is set

put.summary:
Sets one of the cluster's settings (`data-shards`, `parity-shards`,
`repair-after`, `oidc-private-issuers`) for the whole cluster, as
`cairn config set` does. The node answering goes by it right away, the
others within a heartbeat.

get.summary: Whether the console is set up yet (for the sign-in page).

The storage classes a write may name, the warmest first: their names
and ranks only (`/storage` has their pools and layouts, for operators).
Any identity may read them: they're what every S3 client may name in
`x-amz-storage-class`, and listings and HEAD tell them of every object.

put.summary:
Defines a storage class, or changes one, as `cairn class set` does. A
change applies to new objects within a heartbeat, and the packer
rewrites the class's existing data into its new pool and layout over
time.

delete.summary:
Deletes a storage class that holds no data and no uploads, as `cairn
class delete` does. STANDARD can't be deleted.

post.summary:
Has the session act as a session of a role, in its account or another
of the organization's, as STS's AssumeRole would let who it signed in
as (see `switch`), for an hour at most.

delete.summary: Has the session act as who it signed in as again.

get.summary: The account's table buckets (`s3tables:ListTableBuckets`).

post.summary: Makes a table bucket, as CreateTableBucket does.

delete.summary: Deletes a table bucket, as DeleteTableBucket does: an empty one only.

put.summary:
Sets what a table bucket's new tables are encrypted with, as
PutTableBucketEncryption does.

Sets a table bucket's unreferenced file removal, as
PutTableBucketMaintenanceConfiguration does.

post.summary: Makes a namespace in a table bucket, as CreateNamespace does.

delete.summary: Deletes an empty namespace, as DeleteNamespace does.

put.summary:
Sets a table bucket's policy (PutTableBucketPolicy), or deletes it
(DeleteTableBucketPolicy), if it's empty.

Sets a table bucket's new tables' storage class, as
PutTableBucketStorageClass does.

post.summary:
Makes an (empty) Iceberg table, as CreateTable does: without metadata,
which its first writer makes.

delete.summary: Deletes a table, and its files, as DeleteTable does.

get.summary:
A table's maintenance configuration (GetTableMaintenanceConfiguration),
and its jobs' status (GetTableMaintenanceJobStatus).

put.summary: Sets a table's compaction, as PutTableMaintenanceConfiguration does.

Sets a table's snapshot management, as PutTableMaintenanceConfiguration
does.

get.summary: The templates there are.

post.summary:
Makes a template's policies, as IAM's CreatePolicy (with their tags,
TagPolicy too) would: all of them, or none.
What a template would make, used so: nothing is made.

get.summary: The remote tiers, as `cairn tier list` lists them.

post.summary:
Adds a tier, as `cairn tier add` does, once it's reachable and holds
nothing. Its key is made and kept in the database (and so in the
backup), and isn't shown.

put.summary:
Changes a tier, as `cairn tier set` does: new credentials are checked
to reach it first.

delete.summary:
Deletes a tier that no class keeps its data in, and that holds nothing
anymore, as `cairn tier delete` does.

get.summary:
The account's topics the session may see (`sns:ListTopics`), with what
`sns:GetTopicAttributes` shows of each (nothing, if it may not).

post.summary: Makes a topic, as SNS's CreateTopic does.

delete.summary:
Deletes a topic, and its subscriptions, as SNS's DeleteTopic does.
Buckets' configurations naming it stay, and their events are dropped.

put.summary: Sets (or, empty, removes) a topic's delivery policy.
Sets a topic's policy, as SetTopicAttributes does.

post.summary: Publishes a message to a topic's subscriptions (to try them).

put.summary: Sets a topic's display name and signature version.

post.summary:
Subscribes an endpoint to a topic: it's sent a confirmation, whose
`SubscribeURL` (under the console's origin) confirms it.

delete.summary: Unsubscribes a confirmed subscription, as SNS's Unsubscribe does.

put.summary: Sets a topic's tags to these: those it has that aren't are removed.

patch.summary:
Renames or moves a user, as IAM's UpdateUser: allowed on it, and on
where it goes (its new ARN; moved only, its new path: see `iam`).

post.summary: Attaches a managed policy to a user.

delete.summary: Detaches a managed policy from a user.

put.summary:
Sets a user's permissions boundary, as IAM's
PutUserPermissionsBoundary (decided by the boundary asked for).

delete.summary: Removes a user's permissions boundary.

post.summary:
Makes a new access key for a user, with a random ID and secret; a user
has at most two.

put.summary: Lets one of the user's access keys sign requests, or stops it.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the user's access keys.

get.summary: One of the user's inline policies, as it was set.

put.summary: Sets one of the user's inline policies, if it's a valid identity policy.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the user's inline policies.

put.summary: Sets a user's tags, as IAM's TagUser and UntagUser would.

AccessGrant.description: A grant: a grantee's permission on a scope within a location.

AccessGrants.description:
The account's Access Grants: its instance, if it has one, and its
locations and grants, each if they may be seen.

visible.description: Whether the instance may be seen (`s3:GetAccessGrantsInstance`).

parent_id.description: The root's or a unit's ID.

buckets.description: How many buckets it has (which keep it from being closed).

parent_id.description: The organizational unit it's in; none for the root.

grantee.description:
An account's ID (or canonical ID), or a group: `AllUsers` (everyone,
unsigned requests too), `AuthenticatedUsers` (any signed request) or
`LogDelivery` (server access logs).

AclInfo.description: An ACL, of a bucket or an object version.

owner.description: The account that owns what it's on.

user_handle.description: The directory user the passkey is of, as the authenticator says.

AssignmentSummary.description:
A permission set's assignment to a directory user or group, in an
account.

account_id.description: The account it gives the permission set in, by ID.

principal_id.description: The user's or group's ID in the identity store.

principal_name.description: A user's user name, or a group's name.

provider.description: Its identity source; none for Cairn's own directory.

compact.description: Blobs with enough garbage to be compacted.

consolidate.description: Blobs small enough to be consolidated.

convert.description:
Blobs large enough to be coded that aren't in their class's layout,
and blobs outside their class's pool, which the packer converts (see
`packer::Layouts`).

copies.description:
Replicated blobs with more or fewer copies than their class says
(none while that isn't settled), and how many copies the
mover is to add and to drop (see `mover`).

garbage_log.description:
Entries of the garbage log the packer hasn't folded yet: one per blob
that a statement deleted parts from.

moves.description:
Shards to move off nodes being removed, or down for longer than the
`repair-after` setting (see `mover`); and that setting, in minutes (0:
off).

packing.description: Blobs leased by packing jobs, right now.

Backup.description: The backup, if it was ever set up.

BackupEnabled.description: What turning the backup on came to.

location.description: Where it backs up to, in words.

new_key.description:
Whether it made a new key, which a restore needs: `cairn backup key`
on a node shows it, to keep apart from the cluster.

BackupForm.description: Where to back up to, and how, as `cairn backup enable` takes it.

bucket.description:
The bucket: turn versioning on for it, so that it keeps what a
mistake (or an attacker with these credentials) deletes.

interval.description:
How often changes are shipped, e.g. `5m` (the default): the most a
restore can lose.

key.description:
The backup's key (base64, 32 bytes), to use one of one's own;
otherwise the backup keeps its key, or gets a new one.

pack_size.description: How large packs of data are, e.g. `256MiB` (the default).

prefix.description: A prefix of the backup's own.

retention.description: How long what's no longer needed is kept, e.g. `7d` (the default).

secret_access_key.description:
Left out (or empty) to keep the backup's, for the same endpoint and
access key ID.

BackupObjects.description:
The backup's objects of a kind: `journal`, `pack`, `base`, or `tier`
(a tier's objects, which the backup points at but doesn't copy).

unneeded.description: Packs nothing needs anymore, which are kept for the retention.

BackupStatus.description:
Where the backup is, and how far it's got, as `cairn backup status` and
the console show it. Ages are in seconds. Neither its key nor its
credentials' secret are shown.

backfill.description: Parts from before the backup still to copy, while there are any.

base_age.description:
The last complete base's age and size: until there's one, nothing
can be restored.

oneOf.description: The base being built, if one is.

changes.description: Changes captured and not yet shipped.

checked_age.description: How long ago a cycle last ran (found something to ship or not).

interval.description:
Seconds between cycles, how long what's unneeded is kept, and the
bytes of a pack.

journal.description: The last journal's number, and its age, if there's one yet.

last_error.description: The last failure, and its age.

BaseProgress.description: How far the base being built has got.

table.description: The table it's at (from 1), of how many, and its name.

BatchJobDetail.description: A job, as DescribeJob tells it.

oneOf.description: The manifest it generated, once it has (if it's written out).

generator.description: Its manifest generator's settings, if it generates its manifest.

oneOf.description: Its manifest, if it was given one.

operation_settings.description: What the operation does (its tags, retention, target, …).

suspended_cause.description: `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`, while it waits to be confirmed.

BatchJobSummary.description: A job, as lists show it.

operation.description: Its operation, as S3 Control names it (`S3PutObjectTagging`, …).

oneOf.description:
A CSV object of `bucket,key` lines (`bucket,key,versionId` with
version IDs).

etag.description: The object's ETag (what the job is pinned to).

oneOf.description: An inventory report's `manifest.json`.
Generated from a bucket's objects, those its filters pass.

eligible_for_replication.description: Only what its bucket's replication configuration replicates.

output_bucket.description: Where to write the manifest out (empty: it isn't).

BatchManifest.description: Which objects a new job is on.

BatchManifestObject.description: A manifest object: a CSV one, or an inventory report's `manifest.json`.

oneOf.description: Replaces each version's tags (`S3PutObjectTagging`).
`S3DeleteObjectTagging`.
`S3PutObjectRetention`: a mode and a date, or neither to remove it.
`S3PutObjectLegalHold`.
Batch Replication (`S3ReplicateObject`).
`S3PutObjectCopy`, into a bucket, under a prefix.
`S3PutObjectAcl`, a canned ACL.
`S3ComputeObjectChecksum`.
`S3UpdateObjectEncryption`, to SSE-KMS under a key.

BatchOperation.description: What a new job does to each object.

garbage_bytes.description: Bytes of packed blobs that no part references anymore.

Block.description: A public access block's four flags.

arn.description: A managed policy's ARN: the account's own, or one of Cairn's.

BucketAccess.description:
Who may get at a bucket, besides its users' grants and policies: its

oneOf.description:
Its account's public access block, if it has one, which applies to
the bucket as well.

policy.description: Its policy, as GetBucketPolicy shows it; `null` if it has none.

public.description: Whether the policy makes the bucket public.

oneOf.description:
Its public access block; `null` if it has none, or the actor may not
see it (`public_access_block_hidden`).

public_access_block_hidden.description:
Whether the actor may not see the bucket's public access block
(`s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock`): its policy is shown all the same,
so that whoever may change a policy that denies everything else (the
account's root user, say) can.

users.description:
The bucket's account's users whose own policies (inline and
attached) give them access to the whole bucket, and what.

enabled.description:
Whether the bucket has ACLs enabled (its Object Ownership isn't
`BucketOwnerEnforced`); if not, its ACL is its owner's full control.

oneOf.description: `null` if it has none.

`null` if it has none: writes that ask for no encryption aren't

kms.description: Whether the cluster has a KMS, which either needs.

sse_s3.description: Whether it has a key of its own for SSE-S3.

fields.description: The optional fields a configuration may ask for.

BucketLifecycle.description: A bucket's lifecycle rules, if it has any.

oneOf.description: `null` if it logs nothing.

BucketLoggingForm.description: Where a bucket's server access logs go.

date_source.description:
`PartitionedPrefix`: whose date the partitions are, `EventTime` or

key_format.description:

target_bucket.description: The bucket they're written to: one of the same account's.

target_prefix.description: What their keys begin with (may be empty).

events.description: The events a rule may name, in S3's order (in a response).

oneOf.description: What every new version that asks for no retention gets.

enabled.description: Whether the bucket has Object Lock (it can't be disabled again).

ownership.description:
`BucketOwnerEnforced` (ACLs disabled), `BucketOwnerPreferred` or
`ObjectWriter`; `null` if it has no ownership controls, which is as
`ObjectWriter`.

BucketReplication.description: A bucket's replication configuration, and what's queued.

backlog.description: What's queued, by destination (whatever names them now).

oneOf.description: `null` if it has none.

Its account's public access block, if it has one, which applies to
the bucket as well.

default_encryption.description:
Its default encryption, if it has one: `SSE-S3` or `SSE-KMS` (under
`default_kms_key`).

default_kms_key.description:
The KMS key of its default encryption (SSE-KMS), if it has one: what a

object_lock.description: Whether it has Object Lock enabled (see `s3::object_lock`).

objects.description: Current versions that aren't delete markers.

public.description: Whether its policy makes it public (GetBucketPolicyStatus).

oneOf.description: Its public access block, if it has one.

users.description:
The account's users whose policies give them access to the whole
bucket (see `who_has_access`).

BucketVersioning.description: A bucket's versioning, as GetBucketVersioning tells it.

mfa_delete.description:
Whether deleting a version, or changing versioning, needs an MFA
code (`x-amz-mfa`); `null` if it was never set. Only the S3 API
changes it, with one.

oneOf.description: `null` if it has none.

Ceremony.description:
A ceremony's options, for `navigator.credentials` (WebAuthn's JSON form:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` or `…RequestOptionsJSON`), and
the ID of its challenge, to send back with the response.

value.description:
Base64; `null` if it's sealed under a key Cairn doesn't open for
this (SSE-C's, the client's; SSE-KMS's, which takes the KMS).

account_id.description:
The account to act in, by ID: one the set is assigned to the user

name.description: One of the session's permission sets, by name.

ClassChanged.description: What a class's change came to.

description.description: Its pool and layout, in words.

ClassForm.description: A storage class, as the console sets it: all of it, in a pool or a tier.

data_shards.description:
Data shards its blobs over 64 MiB are erasure-coded into (1 keeps
them replicated); none for the `data-shards` setting.

parity_shards.description: Parity shards of its blobs; none for the `parity-shards` setting.

pool.description: The pool its data goes to: nodes' `--data-dir <pool>=<path>`.

rank.description:
Its place in the classes' order, the warmest highest (STANDARD is
0); none for no place.

tier.description:
The remote tier its data goes to, rather than a pool (see `/tiers`):
then it goes by STANDARD's layout, and has no shards of its own.

ClassUsage.description: A storage class, as this node goes by it, and what it holds.

coding.description:
Whether they're brought to it now: it takes as many live nodes with
its pool as shards.

data_shards.description:
Its own data and parity shards, if it sets them (else the
settings').

layout_data_shards.description:
The layout its large blobs are to have: in so many data shards (1:
replicated) and parity shards.

lower_bytes.description:
The bytes of its blobs that belong in lower classes, since lifecycle

misplaced.description: Committed blobs outside its pool, which the packer rewrites into it.

nodes.description: Active nodes with its pool, and of them, the live ones.

rank.description:
Its place in the classes' order, the warmest highest (see
`classes`), if it has one.

remote_blobs.description: Its blobs in tiers, and their bytes.

tier.description:
The remote tier it keeps its data in, if it's a tier's (see `tiers`):
then its pool and layout are STANDARD's, which its data waits in.

state.description:
`active`, `removing` (its shards are moving to other nodes, see
`mover`) or `removed`.

oneOf.description: What the node reported, if it's live and answered.

stats_error.description: Why a live node's stats are missing.

http_error_code_returned_equals.description:

key_prefix_equals.description: `KeyPrefixEquals`: the requests for keys starting with it.

Counts.description: Counts of requests, by how they ended, and of what they moved.

client_errors.description: Answered with a 4xx: the client's fault (including denied requests).

latency_us.description: The sum of the times until the response's head was ready.

server_errors.description: Answered with a 5xx: a fault, or too few nodes.

Coverage.description: How much of the data the scrubber has checked (see `scrub`).

legacy_blobs.description: Committed blobs from before checksums, which can't be checked.

nodes.description:
What each node holds of checksummed data, and how recently it was
checked.

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`); `/` if not given.

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary: a managed policy's ARN.

max_session_duration.description: Its longest session, in seconds (3600 to 43200); 3600 if not given.

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`); `/` if not given.

trust.description: Who may assume it: a trust policy.

access_key.description:
Whether it gets an access key, of a random ID (else it has none

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary: a managed policy's ARN.

groups.description: Groups to add it to, by name (each checked as IAM's AddUserToGroup).

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`); `/` if not given.

policies.description:
Managed policies to attach to it, by ARN (each checked as IAM's
AttachUserPolicy).

Credentials.description: Temporary credentials of a session's role, for the CLI and SDKs.

expiration.description: When they expire (seconds since the epoch).

bucket_key.description:
Whether it asks for a bucket key: told back, but every object has

kms_key_id.description: SSE-KMS: the key, as it's given (its ID, its ARN, or an alias).

DirectoryGroupChange.description: A group of Cairn's own directory, as it's made or changed.

DirectoryGroupSummary.description:

groups.description: Its groups, as the source's group claim said when it signed in.

The permission set it acts as, and the account (by ID) it acts in
there, if it picked one.

permission_sets.description:
The permission sets assigned to it or its groups, in the accounts
they're assigned in, to pick from.

user_id.description: Its ID in the identity store, and its user name there.

DirectoryUserChange.description:
What a user of Cairn's own directory becomes: its attributes as the

user_name.description: Its user name: 1 to 128 characters, no spaces.

DirectoryUserSummary.description: A directory user, as it last signed in.

first_signed_in.description:
When it was first in the identity store, and when it last changed

given_name.description: A user of Cairn's own directory's names (its `Name`'s parts).

groups.description: Its groups, by name (a source's: as its last sign-in said).

id.description: Its ID in the identity store.

passkeys.description:
A user of Cairn's own directory's passkeys, when it last signed in
with one, and whether a setup link for it is out.

provider.description:
Its identity source, and its subject there; none for a user of
Cairn's own directory.

document.description: JSON; for a delivery policy, empty to remove it.

EncryptionInfo.description: How an object version is encrypted (see `s3::sse`).

kind.description:
`SSE-C` (with its client's key, which Cairn doesn't have), `SSE-KMS`

Whose a setup link is, and the options to make a passkey of the

A one-time link for a user of Cairn's own directory to set up a passkey

error.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

bad_blocks.description: How many blocks failed; none if the whole file is at fault.

lost.description:
The object versions (and uploads' parts) with lost bytes, the most

lost_objects.description: How many there are, all told.

recent.description:
Findings of the last day, by node: many of them in a short time are a

Whether some bucket has had no whole sweep yet, so that a round reads

Versions a round of every bucket's sweep reads: the last whole sweep

version_id.description: The version; none for a part of an upload in progress.

url.description: Where to send the browser: the provider's sign-in.

OrganizationOverview.description: The organization's structure and its SCPs.

attachments.description: Which SCPs each target (the root, a unit, an account) has.

root_id.description: The root's ID (`r-…`), which units and accounts are under.

scps_enabled.description: Whether service control policies are enabled.

coding.description:
Whether blobs are brought to that layout now: it takes as many live
nodes as shards.

data_shards.description:
What STANDARD's blobs larger than `small_size` are erasure-coded
into (its data shards, or the `data-shards` setting, and the parity
shards). One data shard: they aren't. Other classes' are in
`classes`.

max_data_shards.description: The most data and parity shards the settings allow.

parity_setting.description:
The `parity-shards` setting, if it's set; else every node goes by its
`--replication-factor`.

PackerTotals.description: What the packer did since the node started.

etag.description: What to complete the upload with.

backed_up.description: Whether it's synced (backed up) by its provider, as it last said.

current.description: Whether this session was signed in with it.

PermissionSetChoice.description: A permission set a directory user may use, in an account.

session_duration.description: How long its sessions (and credentials) last, in seconds.

PermissionSetSummary.description: A permission set: the policies directory users act with, as its role.

account_id.description:
The instance's account (the management account), whose roles the
console's IAM pages show.

attached.description:
Its managed policies: AWS's (Cairn's), and the account's (customer
managed).

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary's ARN, if it has one.

inline_policy.description: Whether it has an inline policy.

provisioned.description: The accounts it's provisioned to (none until it's first assigned).

role_name.description:
The name of its role in each account it's provisioned to (which IAM
can't change).

session_duration.description: How long its sessions (and credentials) last, in seconds.

description.description: Its new description; unchanged if not given.

document.description: Its new document (a new default version); unchanged if not given.

PolicyDocument.description: An inline policy: a JSON document in IAM's policy language.

PolicySummary.description: A managed policy: one of Cairn's (AWS's names), or the account's own.

aws.description: Whether it's one of Cairn's (AWS's), which can't be changed.

bounds.description: The account's users whose permissions boundary it is.

groups.description: The account's groups it's attached to.

role_bounds.description: The account's roles whose permissions boundary it is.

roles.description: The account's roles it's attached to.

users.description: The account's users it's attached to.

tags.description:
All of its tags (keys case-sensitive): those it has of other keys go
(UntagPolicy), the rest are set (TagPolicy).

PolicyVersion.description: One of a managed policy's versions.

default.description: Whether it's the default, which decides.

PoolDisk.description: A pool of a node, and the filesystem of its data dir.

ProviderButton.description: A provider to sign in at.

ProvisionSummary.description: A permission set's provisioning to an account.

latest.description: Whether its role there holds the set as it is now.

QueuedReplication.description: A version of a key queued for one of its destinations.

attempts.description: How many times it was taken to be replicated.

destination.description: The bucket, by its name, or `<remote>:<bucket>`.

failure.description: Why it failed last, if it did, for what may pass.

purge.description: Whether it's a deletion of the version (`DeleteReplication`).

host_name.description: The host redirected to; the request's own, if none.

http_redirect_code.description: The redirect's status, a 3XX but 300; 301, if none.

protocol.description: `http` or `https`; the request's own, if none.

replace_key_prefix_with.description:
What replaces the prefix the condition names (all of a key, if it
names none).

replace_key_with.description: What replaces the key. Not with `replace_key_prefix_with`.

RedirectAll.description: Where every request is redirected to.

protocol.description: `http` or `https`; the request's own, if none.

Registration.description:
What `navigator.credentials.create()` gave the page (its parts, in
base64url).

RemoteForm.description:
A change to a remote: what's left out stays as it is. Its kind can't
change, since the version IDs it was sent are its kind's. A new endpoint
takes the secret access key again.

access_key_id.description:
New credentials. A new access key ID takes its secret; a secret
alone goes with the current ID.

RemoteSummary.description:
A remote, as `cairn remote list` and the console show it. Its secret
access key isn't shown.

buckets.description: The buckets whose replication rules name it.

ReplicaGroup.description:
The committed blobs of `data_shards` data shards (1: replicated) with
`copies` shards in all, `live` of them on live nodes. A blob is readable
with `data_shards` live shards, and as redundant as the cluster's
replication factor asks with `data_shards` + replication factor − 1.

ReplicationBacklog.description: What's queued for one of a bucket's destinations.

destination.description: The bucket, by its name, or `<remote>:<bucket>`.

failure.description: The latest failure of one that's retrying.

queued.description: Versions, delete markers and deletions waiting to be replicated.

retrying.description:
Of them, those that failed for what may pass, and wait to be tried
again.

account.description: The account that must own the bucket, if it's to be checked.

arn.description:
The ARN a remote bucket was named by, if MinIO's or RustFS's form:
kept while it names the same remote and bucket.

kms_key.description:
The KMS key SSE-KMS replicas are encrypted under (`<mount>/<key>`,
or its ARN).

owner_override.description:
Whether replicas are owned by the bucket's owner
(`AccessControlTranslation`), which needs `account`.

remote.description:
The remote (`cairn remote`) the bucket is on, if it isn't in this
cluster.

storage_class.description: The storage class replicas are stored in, if not their source's.

ReplicationForm.description: A replication configuration, as the console edits it.

role.description: The IAM role it replicates as, by its ARN: the bucket's account's.

ReplicationRemote.description:
A registered remote, as a rule names it: never its endpoint or
credentials.

delete_markers.description:
Whether delete markers are replicated (`DeleteMarkerReplication`);
not with tags.

delete_versions.description:
Whether deletions of versions, by their IDs, are replicated: MinIO's
`DeleteReplication`, which S3 hasn't.

kms_objects.description:
Whether SSE-KMS objects are replicated (`SseKmsEncryptedObjects`),
which needs the destination's `kms_key`.

legacy.description:
A rule of S3's first schema: a prefix of its own, no filter by tags,
no priority, and it replicates delete markers. A configuration's
rules are all of one schema.

prefix.description: Only keys with this prefix (empty: all).

priority.description:
Which rule decides where rules overlap: the highest. Ignored for a
rule of S3's first schema (`legacy`).

replica_modifications.description: `ReplicaModifications`, if it's given: kept, without effect.

tags.description: Tags a version must have, with these values.

history.description: The last hour's slots that had requests, oldest first.

ops.description: Since the node started, by operation.

slot_secs.description: How many seconds a slot of `history` covers.

max_session_duration.description: Its longest session, in seconds (3600 to 43200).

RoleSummary.description:
A role: an identity no one signs as with keys of its own, but assumes
(STS's AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity), as its trust policy
allows, for temporary credentials.

id.description: Its unique ID (`AROA…`), which never changes or comes back.

max_session_duration.description: The longest session it allows, in seconds.

policies.description: The names of its inline policies.

trust.description: Its trust policy: who may assume it (as GetRole shows it).

tags.description:
All of its tags: those it has of other keys go (UntagRole), the
rest are set (TagRole).

token.description: The token of the root user's link (after its `#`).

oneOf.description: What requests the rule redirects; all, if none.

expose.description: `ExposeHeader`s: the response headers a page may read.

headers.description: `AllowedHeader`s: what a preflight may ask to send.

max_age.description: `MaxAgeSeconds`: how long a browser may keep a preflight's answer.

base.description: Whether to take a base first.

ScpAttachment.description: An SCP attached to a target.

ScpChange.description: An SCP, as it's made or changed.

content.description:
The policy's JSON, at most 10,240 characters; an Allow statement's
resource is `*` only.

aws_managed.description: AWS's FullAWSAccess, which can't be changed or deleted.

target_id.description: The root's, a unit's or an account's ID.

ScrubTotals.description:
What the scrubber did since the node started: the copies it checked (and
their bytes), how many of them it found damaged or missing, how many of
those it repaired, and how many have data that's intact nowhere, and how
many of its passes failed.

Secret.description: A user's secret, which is shown only this once.

warnings.description:
What's wrong with the cluster's layouts now, if anything: too few
nodes for them, say.

Setup.description: Whether the console is set up yet.

can_sign_in.description:
Whether anyone can sign in: a directory user has a passkey, or
there's an identity source. Until then, the sign-in page says how to
make the first administrator, on a node.

t.description: When the slot starts. The same on every node, so slots add up.

Storage.description:
What's stored where, how well it's replicated, and what the background jobs
still have to do.

classes.description: The storage classes (see `classes`), and what each holds.

StorageClassName.description: A storage class, as a write may name it.

rank.description:
Its place in the classes' order, the warmest highest (STANDARD is 0);
none if it has none.

arn.description:
Its ARN, once it's confirmed; else `PendingConfirmation`, or
`Deleted` (which an old token can still restore).

key.description: The key it has got to.

account.description: The role's account, by its ID.

role.description: The role's name, after its path if it has one (`team/deployer`).

SwitchedMe.description: A role a session switched to.

expires_at.description:
When it ends, and the session acts as who it signed in as again
(seconds since the epoch).

from.description: Who the session signed in as: its ARN.

TableBucketDetail.description: A table bucket, its configuration, and what's in it.

encryption.description: `AES256` or `aws:kms`, and its key, if it may be seen.

policy.description: Its policy (JSON), if it has one (and it may be seen).

oneOf.description: Its tables' unreferenced file removal, if it may be seen.

TableBucketSummary.description: A table bucket, as lists show it.

TableCompaction.description:
A table's compaction: its small files rewritten into files of the
target size, their rows ordered as the strategy says.

TableMaintenance.description:
A table's maintenance, and how its jobs last went (each if it may be
seen).

TableMaintenanceJob.description: How a maintenance job last went.

TableSnapshotManagement.description:
A table's snapshot management: its snapshots beyond the newest
`min_snapshots_to_keep`, and older than `max_snapshot_age_hours`, expire.

TableSummary.description: A table of a table bucket.

metadata_location.description: Its current metadata file, if it has one (and it may be seen).

warehouse_location.description: Where its files are (and it may be seen).

Tag.description:
A tag of a bucket, an object version (see `s3::tags`) or a user (whose
keys are unique regardless of case).

Template.description: A template, as the console lists them.

id.description: Its ID, as a use names it (`template`).

version.description: Its version, which changes when what it makes does.

TierForm.description: A change to a tier: what's left out stays as it is.

access_key_id.description:
New credentials. A new access key ID takes its secret; a secret
alone goes with the current ID.

remote_class.description:
The storage class new objects are written in there; empty for the
service's default.

writable.description: Whether this cluster may write to it and delete from it.

TierSummary.description:
A tier, as `cairn tier list` and the console show it: where it is, and
what it holds. Its credentials' secret and its key aren't shown.

classes.description: The classes that keep their data there.

garbage.description: Its objects that are no longer needed, and are still to be deleted.

objects.description: Its objects, and their live bytes.

remote_class.description:
The storage class its objects are written in there, if not the
service's default.

writable.description:
Whether this cluster writes to it and deletes from it (a restored
cluster's tiers are read-only until it's given them).

delivery_policy.description: Its delivery policy, if it has one of its own (JSON).

effective_delivery_policy.description: What applies: its own, or SNS's defaults (JSON).

TopicSummary.description: A topic, as lists show it.

parent_id.description: Its parent unit; none for the root.

UnreferencedFileRemoval.description:
A table bucket's unreferenced file removal: its tables' files that
nothing references are noncurrent after `unreferenced_days`, and
deleted `non_current_days` after that.

bucket_prefix.description:
The names of its buckets start with this (default: the team's
name, lowercase, and `-`).

list_all_buckets.description:
Whether the team sees every bucket's name
(`s3:ListAllMyBuckets`, which can't be limited to some).

list_policies.description:
Whether its admins see every managed policy's name and path
(`iam:ListPolicies`, which can't be limited to some).

team.description:
The team's name: its path is `/<team>/`, its policies'
names start with it.

buckets.description: A bucket's name, or a pattern (`*` for any characters).

name.description: The policy's name (default: from the buckets and levels).

Use.description: What a template is used with.

UserAccess.description: What a user's policies allow it on a whole bucket.

name.description: Its new name (unique in the account regardless of case).

UserSummary.description: A user, never with its secret.

boundary.description: Its permissions boundary's ARN, which caps what its policies allow.

groups.description: The groups it's in, by name, whose policies are its own too.

id.description: Its ID, which never changes or comes back.

keys.description: Its access keys, oldest first (never their secrets).

path.description: Its path (`/`, or `/…/`), which its ARN has before its name.

policies.description: The names of its inline policies.

tags.description:
All of its tags: those it has of other keys go (UntagUser), the
rest are set (TagUser).

oneOf.description:
Its ACL, if the bucket has ACLs enabled and the actor may read it
(`s3:GetObjectAcl`, an older version's `s3:GetObjectVersionAcl`).

legal_hold.description:
Whether it has a legal hold; `null` if it never had one, or it may
not be read.

oneOf.description: How it's encrypted; none if it isn't.

lost_bytes.description: How many of its parts' bytes are intact on no replica.

replication_status.description:
As `x-amz-replication-status`: `PENDING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or
`REPLICA` (see `replication`); none if it isn't replicated.

Versioning.description:
A bucket's versioning state. A bucket starts out unversioned; once enabled,
it only moves between enabled and suspended. Serialized as it's stored.

Warnings.description:
What's wrong with how things are now, after a change: for the operator
to see, as the CLI prints its warnings.

error_document.description:
`ErrorDocument`'s `Key`: the object served (with the error's status)
for a 4XX error.

index_document.description:
`IndexDocument`'s `Suffix`: what a request for a "directory" (the
root, or a key ending in `/`) is served, appended to its key.

oneOf.description:
`RedirectAllRequestsTo`: every request is redirected there; nothing
else may be set then.

routing_rules.description:
`RoutingRules`: the first one whose condition a request meets
redirects it.
